- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to match upward momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.1) and prices are trending up, model often overcorrects — reduce forecast peak to avoid overshoot.  
- Model frequently overestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative — apply downward bias to first 5–7 days.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overpredicts continuation — cap forecast rise to 5–8% max for next 3 days.  
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model tends to ignore it — add 0.5–1.0 point downward adjustment to next 3–5 days.  
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from negative to positive) is often ignored — model delays response — adjust forecast to reflect sentiment shift within 2–3 days.
